name: Input fields
when: entry = free text AND expected answer fits ONE line AND no fixed option list exists AND the value is not money, a date, a time or a secret — the default text-entry field; beats textarea (proposed "the answer may span multiple lines") whenever the answer is a name, a reference or a phone number; yields to amount-input when the value is money, to date-picker / time-picker when it is a date or time, to secure-entry when it is a one-time code or PIN, and to dropdown or combobox whenever the answer must come from a list at all (Carbon: free text there "is likely to result in an error").
purpose: Text-entry form controls and their label. Family: single-line input (standard + large), multi-line input, date-picker input (with calendar day cells, nav arrows, and a modal/dropdown calendar), and the input label. Full state set: default, hover, active, completed, disabled, error.
$family: Covers the Input fields section; each is a separate Figma component.

$styles: TWO field styles are canon (Dave, 2026-06-22 'both styles exist'): (1) BOXED — full form/border/default box, faithful to node 65570:211753, with optional GBP prefix / trailing icon / (?) help label + 0/100 counter; active & error add a 4px bottom-stroke emphasis on the box. (2) UNDERLINE — bottom-stroke only, no box (the prior canon). Both live in snippets/Input-fields.reference.html.

variants.name: boxed
variants.use: Full-border field (node 65570:211753). Optional prefix (e.g. GBP), trailing icon, (?) help, char counter. Standard + Large. States default/hover/active/completed/disabled/error; active+error keep the 4px bottom-stroke emphasis (black / rag-error). The trailing slot also carries the PASSWORD REVEAL (#314 TP2; Dave 14:55 2026-10-02 call 24, verbatim: "The icon library does have an eye, it might be labeled visible and hidden i think"): a tail-btn with aria-pressed that flips the field's type, drawing global-controls/view while masked and global-controls/hidden while shown; its label states the next action. A page that needs a reveal places this field; it does not draw a Show link of its own.

variants.name: single-line (underline)
variants.use: Bottom-stroke one-line field, no box — the prior canon, kept as the second style (default + Large size).

variants.use: Input that opens a calendar (modal on small screens / dropdown on web). Includes .Date day cells, .Arrow month nav, and the calendar overlay. NOT YET built in the reference — calendar deferred (would add a keyboard grid).

tokens.input-text: text/default @ font-5/medium (value) / font-5/light (placeholder); helper/error text font-7
tokens.label: text/default (input label); disabled text/disabled
tokens.field-background: form/background/default (transparent #ffffff00), hover form/background/hover (#f3f3f3), pressed form/background/pressed (#767676 — date cell)
tokens.date-cell: form/background/* states, form/border/active (selected), text/default, text/reverse (selected), text/disabled
tokens.focus: Keyboard focus only (:focus-visible). A thickened (3px) bottom-stroke in form/border/active — the field's OWN active colour (#000 light / #fff dark), NOT the blue focus/ring and NOT a floating outline (decision: Dave, 2026-06-19, knows the standards). Kept ≥3:1 (1.4.11) and visually distinct from the rest (1px) and error (rag/error) strokes. focus/ring stays the default for ring-pattern components; text inputs use this two-tone-border pattern — see guidelines/focus-indicators.md.

accessibility.label: Every input needs a programmatic label (input-label component); placeholder is not a label
accessibility.error: Error state must pair the red bottom-stroke with a text error message (font-7) and aria-describedby / aria-invalid — not colour alone
accessibility.focus: TWO states. (1) Aesthetic focus, all users: an animated thick bottom-stroke in the field's own colour (form/border/active) grows in. (2) Keyboard focus: that stroke PLUS a prominent accessible ring (outline:none default + outline:2px form/border/active + outline-offset, via :focus-visible), suppressed for pointer via input-modality detection so mouse users keep the clean underline only. Both ≥3:1 (1.4.11). Hover fill clears on focus. See guidelines/focus-indicators.md.
accessibility.stateTreatments: default: 1px form/border/default stroke. focus(keyboard): animated thick form/border/active stroke; hover fill cleared on focus. completed: 3px rag/success stroke + success tick icon. error: 3px rag/error stroke + alert icon INLINE with the value (right of the field), message text in a legible colour (not rag/error — too low on dark), aria-invalid + aria-describedby. disabled: DASHED form/border/disabled underline + text/disabled. (decisions: Dave, 2026-06-19)
accessibility.datePicker: REVIEW (inferred): calendar must be keyboard-navigable (arrow keys, Esc), day cells expose selected/disabled/unavailable states to AT
accessibility.targetArea: Date cells/arrows 40px+; ensure ≥44px hit target where possible

box-bottom-stroke.$note: active (black) / error (rag-error) inner-shadow emphasis on the box.

field-height.$note: single-line; ≥44px target (2.5.8) with breathing room. 'single-line-large' would be taller.

field-padding-inline.$note: underline (bottom-stroke) style — text aligns to the field edge; no inset box.

underline-active.$note: active/focus/error bottom stroke; thicker for visibility.

min-target.$note: WCAG 2.5.8; date cells/arrows must also meet this.

antiPatterns: Using placeholder text as the only label
Showing the error bottom-stroke without an accompanying error message
Leaving the active/error bottom-stroke effects bound to the deprecated tokens — rebind to form/border/active and rag/error (see tokenValidation)

Using outline:none on :focus without a visible replacement, or showing the focus indicator on mouse :focus (use :focus-visible so it appears for keyboard users only), or reusing the red error stroke as the focus indicator — keyboard focus is a thickened form/border/active stroke kept distinct from the error stroke; see guidelines/focus-indicators.md

Binding the field surface to form/background/default in dark mode as-is — it resolves to opaque #FFFFFF (alpha lost), producing a white field with invisible white text; form/* needs dark-mode reconciliation (see tokenValidation)
